samples.summary: Toolbar block-level mutators (`applyBlockStyle`, `toggleList`, `indent`, `outdent`) still write once per selected block with no `doc.batch()`, so the #1045 data loss this change fixes for the keyboard paths survives on the toolbar
samples.evidence:
This change batched the TextEditor keyboard twins — `handleTab` (text-editor.ts:2772), `handleIndent` (2820), `handleOutdent` (2844) — and the toolbar's inline-style path (`applyStyleImpl`, editor.ts:1260/1267). But the sibling `EditorAPI` members in editor.ts are untouched and still loop `forEachBlockInSelection` with a store write inside and no batch:

- `applyBlockStyle` (editor.ts:3451-3455): `docStore.snapshot(); forEachBlockInSelection(block => doc.applyBlockStyle(block.id, style));`
- `toggleList` (3612-3624): `doc.setBlockType(...)` per block
- `indent` (3632-3649) and `outdent` (3656-3674): `doc.setBlockType(...)` / `doc.applyBlockStyle(...)` per block

Each `doc.*` call is one `store` write, and on `YorkieDocStore` one write outside a batch is one `doc.update()` and therefore one undo-stack entry (`withUpdate`, yorkie-doc-store.ts:2972-2980). That is exactly the shape the new `withUndoUnit` doc comment describes: past Yorkie's 50-entry `MaxUndoRedoStackDepth` `pushUndo` shifts the OLDEST entries off, so over a >50-block selection the earliest blocks' change becomes permanently un-undoable.

All four are reachable from normal UI, not internal-only: `editor.applyBlockStyle({ alignment })` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:566, 743), `editor.applyBlockStyle({ lineHeight })` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:517), `editor?.toggleList(...)` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:941/945, text-paragraph-group.tsx:176/194), `editor?.indent()/outdent()` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:949/953, text-paragraph-group.tsx:212/230).

Net effect: pressing Tab batches, clicking the identical Increase-indent toolbar button does not — and the new frontend test file only pins the keyboard variants plus `editor.applyStyle`, so nothing catches it. Same untouched shape at editor.ts:3702 (`insertLink` cell-range → `applyStyleToCellRange` unbatched) and editor.ts:4243-4254 (`applyTableCellStyle` cell-range loop, one write per cell).
searchedFor: Read text-editor.ts:2760-2860 to confirm the keyboard twins were batched
Read yorkie-doc-store.ts:2960-3022 (withUpdate / batch = one doc.update per write)

samples.summary: Adding `readOnly` to the notes effect deps makes the effect re-run, but its cleanup never disposes `YorkieNoteStore`, whose constructor subscription cannot be released — the exact leak `docs-view` fixed with `store.dispose()`
samples.evidence:
`YorkieNoteStore`'s constructor calls `doc.subscribe(...)` and discards the returned unsubscribe (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.ts:143-147); the class exposes no `dispose()`. notes-view.tsx's cleanup (lines 150-155) only does `editor.dispose(); storeRef.current = null;`.

Before this change the effect ran once per document, so the leak was invisible. With `readOnly` in the deps (line 167) an `editor` → `viewer` downgrade from `/shared/:token` re-runs the effect: a second `YorkieNoteStore` is built over the *same* Yorkie document (which belongs to the enclosing provider and outlives the effect), and the first store stays subscribed to `local-change`/`undoredo` forever, calling `captureHistorySelection()` on a store nothing reads. This is the identical hazard the diff calls out for docs (`store.dispose()` added at docs-view.tsx:574) and that slides already handles (`store.dispose()` at slides-view.tsx:1216); notes is the one of the three left without it.
searchedFor: Read slides-view.tsx:1181-1237 and docs-view.tsx:549-590 for comparison

samples.summary: `snapshot()` no longer clears redo, so an action that snapshots but writes nothing leaves a live undo checkpoint on top of a preserved redo stack — a dead Cmd+Z followed by a dead Cmd+Shift+Z
samples.evidence:
`snapshot()` now only `pushUndo()`s (memory.ts:214-220); redo is cleared by `willWrite()` on the first mutation instead. Several paths call `saveSnapshot()` and can then write nothing: `TextEditor.handleTab` returns without any `setBlockType` when every selected item is already at level 0/8 (text-editor.ts:2771-2785), `handleBackspace` returns at the start of the first block in a cell after `saveSnapshot()` (text-editor.ts:2513/2542), `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` similarly.

Sequence on `MemDocStore`: state A, write, `undo()` → `redo=[B]`, `undo=[]`. Now such an action runs: `snapshot()` pushes A → `undo=[A]`; nothing is written so `willWrite()` never fires and `redo` stays `[B]`. `canUndo()` is now true for a checkpoint identical to the current document, so Cmd+Z changes nothing and pushes a duplicate A onto redo (`undo()`, memory.ts:172-176), making the next Cmd+Shift+Z a no-op too. The empty-`batch()` `priorRedo` restore (memory.ts:299) deliberately preserves redo for exactly this case, so the two mechanisms combine here rather than cancelling.
searchedFor: Read packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts hunks in the diff for a covering case

samples.summary: `canUndo()`'s "mark gone" latch cannot actually distinguish a shifted-off floor entry from a rebuilt one, so a rebuilt entry at cap silently discards the undo floor permanently
samples.evidence: At yorkie-doc-store.ts:3058-3073 the code reasons: identity was proven at mark time, so a missing mark means either "shifted off the bottom" or "the SDK rebuilt it in place", and `stack.length >= YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` tells them apart. It does not: a long editing session sits AT the cap (50) most of the time, so a rebuilt-in-place entry observed while the stack is full takes the permissive branch, latches `undoFloorMark = null; undoFloorDepth = 0; undoFloorIdentityUsable = false`, and from then on `canUndo()` returns `true` unconditionally (line 3045). The floor exists because "Yorkie's CRDT redo of writeFullDocument can conflict with subsequent text insertions" and undoing past the load "would destroy blocks the cursor still references" (constructor comment, lines 663-666) — so the latch is one-way into precisely the state the floor was added to prevent. `YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` is also a hard-coded mirror of an unexported SDK constant, so if the real cap is larger the comparison never fires and if it is smaller the branch fires early.
searchedFor: Read the two new frontend tests for canUndo in tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts

samples.summary: `isRevokedShareLinkError` treats every non-408/429 4xx as the server's verdict on the link, including statuses that come from infrastructure rather than the share-link handler
samples.evidence: `resolveShareLink` is a plain unauthenticated `fetch` (share-links.ts:102-110), yet `isRevokedShareLinkError` returns true for the whole 4xx band minus 408/429. A 403 emitted by a CDN/WAF or a proxy in front of the API (a common response for a blocked or bot-flagged request), or a 400 from a malformed proxy rewrite, is not a verdict on the link — but `SharedDocumentByToken`'s `fatal` check (shared-document.tsx:1138-1140) then tears down a live editing session and shows "Link unavailable", which is exactly the data-loss outcome the helper's own doc comment says it exists to avoid. It also disables the single retry (`retry` at shared-document.tsx:1127-1128), so one such response is enough.
searchedFor: Read the new packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.test.ts expectations in the diff

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: the four EditorAPI block-level mutators write once per selected block with no batch. editor.ts:3451-3458 (applyBlockStyle), 3612-3631 (toggleList), 3632-3654 (indent), 3656-3677 (outdent) each do `docStore.snapshot()` then per-block `doc.applyBlockStyle`/`doc.setBlockType` inside `forEachBlockInSelection` (1665+), and the only `batch(` occurrences in editor.ts are 1260/1267/1308 (the inline-style path). No indirect batching exists: MUTATING_METHODS (1044-1054) feeds only neuterMutations (1063-1074, used at 4482/4551), the sole Proxy is pageSetupGuardedStore (3315), Doc.applyBlockStyle (model/document.ts:645-646) delegates unbatched, and no frontend caller wraps them (`batch` appears nowhere in frontend/src/app/docs outside yorkie-doc-store.ts nor in components/text-formatting; call sites docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:517/566/743/941-953, text-paragraph-group.tsx:43/176/194/212/230 call bare). On YorkieDocStore each write is its own doc.update (withUpdate 2972-2980) because snapshot() is a documented no-op (3024-3027), and the 50-entry cap with shift-oldest (570, 588-600) makes the earliest blocks' writes permanently un-undoable on large selections; below the cap it is still one Ctrl+Z per block, leaving a partially reverted document. The repo's own design doc confirms the gap verbatim (docs/design/docs/docs-collaboration.md:313-321, "still issue an unbatched write per block … lose their oldest writes exactly as the keyboard paths did before #1045", tracked as #1048) — known/deferred, but per this lens pre-existing untouched code is still a defect if real. Found no counterexample.
